Approach refuted and reverted; the cost problem re-filed as na-vbe with the shape a fix must have. The ranking rule predicts citation worse than chance - 0.43 of citations in its top four against 0.50 for noise - and the one fact cited in 20 of 20 decisions ranked fifth of eight. Generalisable finding recorded in docs/quipu-integration.md: grounding is one fact per option, so top-k truncation removes the explanation of an option rather than removing information, and an unexplained option loses; any such truncation biases the choice whatever it ranks by. fairness stamps only what the engine knows - is_human(faction) and *DiffLevel - with an explicitly EMPTY handicaps list, and the orchestrator derives the ledger from those two inputs.

## Method

Two thinker.dll builds replaying ONE identical save. No brain, no model, no spend.

    gross  2929637  energy_surplus_total                                     dll f31625a3
    net    0722b7b  energy_surplus_total + turn_commerce_income - facility_maint_total
                                                                             dll e2dbc9e5

old - new == facility_maint_total - turn_commerce_income by construction, so any pair with

56 of 69 matched pairs have old > new. Largest proven facility_maint_total >= 70 (University,

## CORRECTION to this bead's title — "systematically optimistic" is too strong

The exception is our own faction. For Gaians, 11 of 12 distinct pairs run the OTHER way: the gross
value was too LOW, by as much as 74 (473 -> 547). Gaians is commerce-heavy, and the old expression
excluded commerce as well as maintenance, so the sign depends on which dominates.

    Gaians      old too LOW  (commerce > maint)   11 of 12 distinct pairs
    Hive        old too HIGH                       1 of 2  (other cancels 0 -> 0)
    University  old too HIGH                       6 of 7

Honest statement: the gross value is systematically WRONG, in a direction that VARIES BY FACTION —
optimistic where maintenance dominates, pessimistic where commerce does. On the faction we
actually play it erred toward OVERstating the setback.

This does not weaken the fix and is not a refutation of it. RATE_OF maps energy_reserves ->
energy_income, reserves move by net, and net is what the new expression computes. The justification

THE REFRAMING THAT MADE IT SMALL. I began designing a way to DEFER a decision inside the engine's
cycle. Stiwi pointed out that a player can select any unit or base and command it directly,
without waiting for the cycle — so there are two doors, and we had only ever used the one where
the engine asks. Door 2 already existed, already had a result channel, and was used for
everything except orders. Deferral was never needed; it was a workaround for a constraint that
does not bind.

I dropped the door-1 revision trick from the plan rather than keeping it alongside — it is a
second way to do something door 2 does better, and keeping it would have been the more expensive
path chosen because I found it first.

## WHAT I GOT WRONG, on the record

I claimed three times — here, in the doc, and in a commit message — that world views are
fog-gated and orders bypass that path. Measured: fog.py gates the foreign-DIPLOMACY feed only,
and no tile-visibility model existed anywhere. Orders did not slip past a map gate; that gate had
never existed. "Route orders through the existing gate" was not a task, and stating it that way
would have sent whoever picked it up hunting for a gate to reuse.

Phase 4 therefore BUILDS the gate rather than connecting to one: `move` refuses an unexplored
destination via the engine's own is_known. It does not make an agent's knowledge fog-clean —
knowledge arrives in the world view and is that path's problem — it stops the concrete cheat
available through this door.

A second, smaller one: a WorldView field access. The contract is extra="allow" and pydantic
raises AttributeError for an ABSENT extra rather than returning None, so `world_view.faction_id`
worked on every adapter record and exploded on the hand-written fixtures that omit it. 23 test
failures, none in the shape production sends. The failure surfaced only on the inputs least like
production, which is the reverse of the usual asymmetry.

## LIMIT, stated plainly

None of this has met a real turn. The tests are unit tests with a fake adapter, the wire suite
proves the HTTP client and not the game loop, and every "verified live" above means JSON posted
by curl to a running service. na-1g7 carries the live exercise and names the property most likely
to be wrong: order/decision mutual exclusion rests on the decision wait not pumping messages, and
nothing asserts it.
